_meta.indication: FANAPT is indicated for the acute treatment of schizophrenia in adults.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study ILP3005ST (6-week placebo- and active-controlled trial)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multi-center international study; two iloperidone dose groups (12-16 mg/day and 20-24 mg/day) plus risperidone 6-8 mg/day for assay sensitivity and placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults who met DSM-III/IV criteria for schizophrenia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Day 42 (LOCF) in the 18-item BPRS extracted from the PANSS total score; primary comparison iloperidone 12-16 mg/day vs placebo.
pivotal_trials.n: n=706 (iloperidone 12-16 mg/day N=244, iloperidone 20-24 mg/day N=145, risperidone 6-8 mg/day N=157, placebo N=160)
pivotal_trials.result: BPRS LS mean change: iloperidone 12-16 mg/day 7.1 (difference vs placebo 2.1 [95% CI -0.3, 4.5], p=0.090) and 20-24 mg/day 8.6 (difference 3.5 [95% CI 0.8, 6.2], p=0.010) vs placebo 5.0. On the FDA primary analysis the 12-16 mg/day dose did not separate from placebo (p=0.09), so the 20-24 mg/day dose was not formally tested; the review concluded this was a negative study based on the primary analysis.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study VP-VYV-683-3101 (4-week placebo- and active-controlled trial)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multi-center study in India and the United States; randomized 2:1:1 to iloperidone 24 mg/day, ziprasidone 160 mg/day, or placebo; double-blind phase 4 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults who met DSM-III/IV criteria for schizophrenia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline on PANSS total score at the end of treatment (Day 28)
pivotal_trials.n: n=604 (4-week trial) / 606 randomized (iloperidone 24 mg/day, ziprasidone 160 mg/day, placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: PANSS total score LS mean change: iloperidone 24 mg/day -12.0 (difference vs placebo -4.9 [95% CI -8.5, -1.4], p=0.007) vs placebo -7.1; the 24 mg/day FANAPT dose was superior to placebo in the PANSS total score.

key_safety: Commonly observed adverse reactions (incidence ≥5% and two-fold greater than placebo) were dizziness, dry mouth, fatigue, nasal congestion, orthostatic hypotension, somnolence, tachycardia, and weight increased. Tachycardia occurred in up to 12% (FANAPT 20-24 mg/day) vs 1% placebo; dry mouth up to 10% vs 1% placebo; weight increased 9% vs 1% placebo. Somnolence/sedation was reported in 11.9% of patients on ≥10 mg/day vs 5.3% on placebo.
target_moa: Atypical antipsychotic; efficacy proposed to be mediated through a combination of dopamine type 2 (D2) and serotonin type 2 (5-HT2) antagonism, with high affinity binding to 5-HT2A, D2 and D3 receptors.

boxed_warning.content: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis: elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotic drugs are at an increased risk of death (1.6 to 1.7 times placebo). FANAPT is not approved for use in patients with dementia-related psychosis.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an advisory committee because the drug is not the first in its class, the clinical study design was acceptable, and the safety/efficacy data did not pose particular concerns.

summary.text: FANAPT (iloperidone) was approved under a standard 505(b) NDA for the acute treatment of schizophrenia in adults. The application was first submitted September 27, 2007 and received a Not Approvable letter on July 25, 2008; the November 6, 2008 complete response led to approval. No advisory committee was convened. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority review designation is documented.

basis.text: Not Approvable (dated 7-25-08) based on lack of sufficient effectiveness data and lack of sufficient safety data, including concern over prominent QT prolongation and difficulty titrating to an effective dose.

citations.quote: This NDA was first submitted 9-27-07. We issued a Not Approvable letter on 7-25-08.
In our 7-25-08 not approvable letter, we expressed concerns about the remaining 3 short-term studies, all in patients with a mix of schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder.
We also noted in the not approvable letter our concerns about the prominent QT prolonging effect of iloperidone and the difficulty in titrating patients to an effective dose of iloperidone.
